definition: a coin of the United States and Canada worth ten cents

collocations.example: The boy found a shiny dime on the sidewalk yesterday.
We fixed everything ourselves and did not pay a dime.

definition: a small dent or mark on the surface of something

collocations.example: Someone left a ding in the door of my car.
Phones often get a ding when they drop on concrete.

definition: dark, dirty, and not fresh or bright

collocations.example: They rented a dingy room above a noisy downtown bar.
The old white curtains had started to look dingy and gray.

definition: a highly poisonous chemical that can pollute the environment

collocations.example: Long-term dioxin exposure can cause serious harm to human health.
Burning certain plastics can release dioxin into the surrounding air.

definition: to officially refuse to allow or accept something

collocations.example: The referee decided to disallow the goal for offside.
The company may disallow any claim without proper receipts.

definition: to say that you know nothing about something or are not responsible for it

collocations.example: The minister tried to disavow responsibility for the failed project.
He quickly moved to disavow the statement his aide had made.

definition: to pay out money, especially from a large fund

collocations.example: The charity will disburse funds to families after the flood.
The bank agreed to disburse the loan in three stages.

definition: to get off a ship, plane, or other vehicle

collocations.example: Passengers began to disembark from the ferry once it docked.
We were told to disembark at the next port of call.

definition: seeming to come from someone who is not present or has no body

collocations.example: A disembodied voice announced the next train on the platform.
In the film, a disembodied hand crawls slowly across the floor.

definition: to take away someone's right to vote or their rights as a citizen

collocations.example: Critics say the new rules could disenfranchise thousands of poor voters.
The law would disenfranchise an entire group of ordinary citizens.

definition: to make someone lose hope, confidence, or energy

collocations.example: Don't let one small failure dishearten you so quickly.
Do not be easily disheartened by early failures.

definition: (of hair, clothes, or appearance) untidy and messy

collocations.example: He arrived late with disheveled hair and a wrinkled shirt.
She looked tired and disheveled after the long overnight flight.

definition: loss of honor, respect, or a good reputation

collocations.example: His crime brought dishonor on his entire family name.
He chose death over a life of shame and dishonor.

definition: something that makes people not want to do something

collocations.example: High taxes can be a disincentive to working longer hours.
The long waiting list acts as a disincentive to new patients.

definition: not faithful or loyal to a person, group, or country

collocations.example: He was accused of being disloyal to his old friends.
A disloyal employee shared company secrets with a competitor.

definition: to refuse to do what a person, rule, or law tells you to do

collocations.example: Soldiers who disobey orders can face serious punishment.
Students who disobey the rules will be sent to the principal.

definition: not influenced by strong emotion; calm and fair

collocations.example: As a dispassionate observer, she judged the whole case fairly.
The report offered a dispassionate analyzis of the two options.

definition: making you lose hope, energy, or enthusiasm

collocations.example: Losing the final match was a dispiriting experience for everyone.
The endless bad news was deeply dispiriting for the staff.

definition: to make someone feel annoyed or not satisfied

collocations.example: Not wishing to displease her, he avoided answering the question.
Poor service can quickly displease even your most loyal customers.

definition: quiet and easy to control or manage

collocations.example: The old horse was gentle and docile around young children.
The new recruits were expected to be docile and obedient.

definition: a female deer, rabbit, or similar animal

collocations.example: A doe and her fawn grazed quietly at the forest edge.
The startled doe leaped across the road in front of us.

definition: to love someone so much that you cannot see their faults

collocations.example: They dote on their grandchildren and spoil them far too much.
Grandparents often dote endlessly, giving gifts every week.

definition: looking or sounding serious, unfriendly, and gloomy

collocations.example: The teacher gave us a dour expression and said nothing.
He sat in the corner, dour and silent, all evening.

definition: money or property that a bride's family gives to her husband at marriage

collocations.example: Her father promised a large dowry to the groom's family.
In some cultures, a bride must bring a dowry to her marriage.

definition: (of laws or rules) extremely harsh and severe

collocations.example: The government passed draconian laws to control public protests.
Critics called the government's new draconian measures unnecessary.

definition: a large insect with a long thin body and two pairs of transparent wings

collocations.example: A bright red dragonfly landed gently on the pond reeds.
We watched a dragonfly hover above the still green water.

definition: to let saliva fall from the mouth

collocations.example: The sleeping baby began to drool on the soft pillow.
The smell of fresh bread made the hungry dog drool.

definition: a person who does hard, boring, or unpleasant work

collocations.example: She felt like a household drudge after cleaning all day.
He worked like a drudge to pay for his studies.

definition: a priest in the ancient Celtic religion

collocations.example: An ancient druid was believed to understand the secrets of nature.
Visitors gathered at dawn to watch the druid ceremony begin.

definition: a small ball of dough, often filled with meat or vegetables, that is cooked

collocations.example: She ordered a plate of steamed dumplings for the table.
We shared a hot bowl of dumplings on the cold night.

definition: a dark underground prison, especially in a castle

collocations.example: The prisoner was kept in a dark dungeon for years.
The king ordered his enemies thrown into the dungeon.

definition: the first part of the small intestine, just below the stomach

collocations.example: The doctor found an ulcer in the patient's duodenum.
Stomach acid can damage the delicate wall of the duodenum.

definition: a house or apartment that is divided into two separate living spaces

collocations.example: They bought a small duplex apartment near the city center.
The young couple decided to rent a duplex downtown.

definition: threats or force used to make someone do something

collocations.example: He signed the confession only under duress.
Her lawyer made a claim of duress during the trial.

definition: the quality of being full of energy, new ideas, and the power to make things happen

collocations.example: The city is known for its economic dynamism and rapid growth.
Her youthful dynamism brought new energy to the old company.

definition: a machine that turns mechanical energy into electricity

collocations.example: The old bicycle dynamo powered a small front light.
The dynamo generates electricity as the wheel turns.

definition: the distance within which you can hear someone or something

collocations.example: She waited until the children were within earshot to speak.
We moved out of earshot before discussing the surprise party.

definition: a level or rank in an organization, profession, or society

collocations.example: She reached the upper echelons of the company quickly.
He slowly rose through the echelons of the military.

definition: an official order or command given by a person in authority

collocations.example: The emperor issued an edict banning all foreign books.
A royal edict ordered every citizen to pay the new tax.

definition: a model or image of a person, often burned as a form of protest

collocations.example: Angry protesters gathered to burn an effigy of the leader.
The museum displayed a wax effigy of the famous queen.

definition: a mineral in your body, such as sodium, that helps control important body functions

collocations.example: Sports drinks help athletes replace lost electrolytes after hard exercise.
An electrolyte imbalance can make you feel weak and dizzy.

definition: a very large North American deer with big branching antlers

collocations.example: A large herd of elk crossed the snowy mountain valley.
A bull elk stood proudly at the edge of the forest.

definition: facing many problems, difficulties, or attacks

collocations.example: The embattled president faced growing calls to resign.
The embattled government struggled to pass its new budget.

definition: to steal money that you are responsible for or that belongs to your employer

collocations.example: The accountant was caught trying to embezzle company funds.
He was jailed for embezzling from his own clients.

definition: to decorate something with a design, name, or symbol in a very noticeable way

collocations.example: They emblazon a bright logo on every team jersey.
Protesters emblazon their banners with a bold slogan.

definition: to decorate a surface with a raised design or pattern

collocations.example: The craftsman will emboss a design on the leather cover.
They emboss the paper to create a raised company seal.

definition: keeping a title as an honor after retiring, especially a professor

collocations.example: He is now a professor emeritus at a well-known university.
After retiring, she was named chairman emeritus of the board.

definition: the quality of being famous, important, and respected

collocations.example: The young scientist rose to eminence through her brilliant work.
He reached a position of eminence in the medical field.

definition: a person sent as a representative to deliver a message or carry out a mission

collocations.example: The president sent a special emissary to the peace talks.
The king decided to send an emissary to the enemy camp.

definition: causing strong feelings; relating to the emotions

collocations.example: Immigration remains a highly emotive issue in many countries.
The speaker used emotive language to move the whole crowd.

definition: a large Australian bird that cannot fly and runs very fast

collocations.example: The farmer collected a large green emu egg from the nest.
A flightless emu can still run very fast across open land.

definition: to change information into a secret code so others cannot read it

collocations.example: The system will encrypt the data before sending it online.
You should fully encrypt your laptop to protect private files.

definition: to make it difficult for someone to move or do something; to burden

collocations.example: They did not want to encumber the company with debt.
Heavy winter clothing can encumber your movement on the slopes.

definition: a strong feeling of hatred or opposition between people

collocations.example: He felt a deep enmity toward his former business partner.
The enmity between the two tribes lasted for generations.

definition: the very great size, seriousness, or scale of something bad

collocations.example: She was shocked by the enormity of the disaster.
Only later did he understand the full enormity of his mistake.

definition: the scientific study of insects

collocations.example: She decided to study entomology at a famous research university.
Forensic entomology uses insects to help solve serious crimes.

definition: feeling so interested or delighted that you give something all your attention

collocations.example: The children were entranced by the magician's clever tricks.
The audience sat entranced throughout the entire performance.

definition: to twist or wrap two or more things together

collocations.example: The young couple entwine their fingers while walking together.
The green vines entwine around the old wooden fence.

definition: a brain condition that causes a person to have seizures

collocations.example: She has suffered from epilepsy since she was a child.
Daily medicine helps many patients control their epilepsy.

definition: a word or short phrase used to describe a person or thing

collocations.example: The city's heat earned it the epithet 'the furnace.'
His bravery made him deserve the epithet 'the fearless.'

definition: a perfect example of a particular quality or type

collocations.example: The actress was the epitome of elegance on the red carpet.
That phone is considered the epitome of modern design.

definition: the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, written E or ε

collocations.example: Students learned to write the letter epsilon in Greek class.
Mathematicians often use a tiny epsilon to mean a small amount.

definition: relating to horses or the activity of riding horses

collocations.example: She won a gold medal in an equestrian event last year.
Equestrian sports require both skill and a close bond with horses.

definition: the study of how to design equipment and workspaces for comfort and efficiency

collocations.example: Good ergonomics can reduce back pain for office workers.
The company spent money improving office ergonomics for its staff.

definition: a moving staircase that carries people between floors of a building

collocations.example: We took the escalator up to the third floor.
She stumbled on the crowded escalator during the evening rush.

definition: a colorless liquid that burns easily, once used to make people unconscious for surgery

collocations.example: The whiff of ether filled the small operating room.
The cloth was soaked in ether to numb the patient.

definition: extremely delicate, light, and beautiful in a way that seems not of this world

collocations.example: The singer's ethereal voice filled the quiet old church.
The dancer moved with an almost ethereal beauty on stage.

definition: a person who is moved from a dangerous place to a safe one

collocations.example: The flood evacuee stayed in a shelter for several weeks.
Local schools were opened to house evacuees from the fire.

definition: to officially exclude someone from membership of a church

collocations.example: The church decided to excommunicate the rebellious young priest.
The bishop threatened to excommunicate anyone who disobeyed the order.

definition: a person chosen to carry out the instructions in someone's will

collocations.example: She was named the executor of her late uncle's will.
You should appoint a trusted executor to handle your estate.

definition: to officially state that someone is not guilty or to blame

collocations.example: New evidence helped exonerate the accused man completely.
The report will exonerate the pilot from any blame.

definition: (of a price or amount) much too high; unreasonable

collocations.example: Tourists often pay exorbitant prices for food near the beach.
The lawyer charged an exorbitant fee for a simple case.

definition: to make a process happen more quickly

collocations.example: We hired more staff to expedite the approval process.
They paid extra to expedite delivery of the package.

definition: to explain an idea or piece of writing in detail

collocations.example: The professor took an hour to explicate the difficult poem.
She tried to explicate the meaning of the new law.

definition: a large public exhibition or trade show

collocations.example: Thousands of companies showed their products at the trade expo.
The city will hold a huge technology expo next spring.

definition: (of the government) to officially take private property for public use

collocations.example: A government should not expropriate private property without a good reason.
The ruler tried to expropriate land from poor village farmers.

definition: a large, elaborate, and spectacular entertainment or event

collocations.example: The show was a dazzling musical extravaganza with hundreds of dancers.
The mall hosted a weekend shopping extravaganza with huge discounts.

definition: to free someone or something from a difficult situation or a trap

collocations.example: She struggled to extricate herself from the awkward conversation.
Rescuers worked to extricate the driver from the wreckage.

definition: coming from outside; not part of the basic nature of something

collocations.example: Money is a common form of extrinsic motivation at work.
The old painting has both extrinsic value and personal meaning.

definition: a temperature scale on which water freezes at 32 degrees and boils at 212 degrees

collocations.example: The thermometer read ninety degrees Fahrenheit in the shade.
Most Americans still use the Fahrenheit scale for the weather.

definition: a short, loud tune played on trumpets to announce something important

collocations.example: The grand ceremony began with a fanfare of trumpets.
A royal fanfare announced the arrival of the queen.

definition: paying very careful attention to detail; hard to please

collocations.example: He is very fastidious about keeping his desk perfectly clean.
She planned the wedding with fastidious attention to every detail.

definition: relating to cats, or like a cat

collocations.example: She moved across the room with smooth feline grace.
The old woman lived alone with one quiet feline companion.

definition: a low, flat area of wet, marshy land

collocations.example: Rare birds nest in the quiet marshy fen each spring.
Farmers worked for years to drain the fen for crops.

definition: a plant with a crunchy bulb and seeds used in cooking, with a mild licorice flavor

collocations.example: She added fennel seeds to the slow-cooked pork dish.
He sliced a fresh bulb of fennel for the salad.

definition: (of an animal) living in a wild state, especially after escaping from a home or farm

collocations.example: A feral cat had been living under the old porch.
Without owners, the dogs quickly went feral in the hills.

definition: to decorate something with hanging chains of flowers, lights, or ribbons

collocations.example: They festoon the hall with fresh garlands before the feast.
The whole street was festooned with colorful flags.

definition: a special outdoor celebration, party, or festival

collocations.example: The whole village gathered for the summer fete on Saturday.
The school will hold a fete to raise money for books.

definition: an official order given by someone in authority, without discussion

collocations.example: The rules were changed by fiat, without asking the staff.
He could not solve the whole crisis by presidential fiat alone.

definition: often changing, especially in loyalty or affection; not reliable

collocations.example: The spring weather here is notoriously fickle and hard to predict.
Pop stars must deal with a fickle public that changes fast.

definition: a small statue of a person or animal, used for decoration

collocations.example: A fragile china figurine stood on the fireplace mantel.
He loves to collect figurines of famous movie characters.

definition: a young female horse

collocations.example: The young filly galloped happily around the green field.
They plan to race the filly for the first time.

definition: happening in short, irregular periods; not steady or continuous

collocations.example: He got only a few hours of fitful sleep last night.
The rain fell in fitful bursts throughout the afternoon.

definition: (of a bad action) very obvious and shocking; openly done

collocations.example: The decision was a flagrant violation of the agreement.
He showed a flagrant disregard for other people's safety.

definition: easily set on fire

collocations.example: Gasoline is highly flammable, so keep it away from flames.
Store all flammable materials in a cool, safe place.
